result.title: One Patch, Many Policies: Object-Associated Physical Patch Attacks on Robotic Manipulation
result.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) are vulnerable to adversarial visual interference, motivating the study of universal and transferable physical patch attacks. We propose Object-Associated Patch Attack (OAPA), a universal and transferable physical patch framework that enables an attacker to select which task object's manipulation to disrupt through patch placement, without re-optimizing the patch. Our framework combines object-associated placement, differentiable physical compositing, and final action-expert representation divergence. Physical compositing accounts for perspective and occlusion across camera views, while representation divergence guides patch optimization using either relative RMS or cosine distance. Experimental results demonstrate strong attack transferability across task suites and policies, together with the ability to selectively disrupt manipulation of an attacker-chosen task object through patch placement.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 OAPA 物理补丁攻击框架，通过物体关联的放置策略、可微物理合成（视角与遮挡）以及动作专家表示散度（相对 RMS 或余弦距离）来优化通用补丁，使攻击者仅靠贴放位置即可选择干扰哪个任务物体的操作。
AI.relevance_reason: 该攻击以动作专家内部表示散度为目标，且贴放位置可定向选通特定物体的视觉证据，与「局部视觉细节是否被 VLA 内部状态因果使用」及视觉证据筛选问题有具体联系，可供核查其跨策略迁移是否揭示表示层面的证据旁路。
